svg.title: Choice Brier: all models and a separate detail view
svg.desc: Choice Brier = mean over 12 labeled answers of the sum of five squared errors, range 0 to 2; sorted lowest first with exact ties in captured order. API models are orange and prefixed API. Jev 1.13 (OpenRouter): 0; Lumma-Fev-9B: 4.1128335667e-05; Circuit-8B: 0.000473245736627; CLEF (Cloudflare): 0.000691023333333; Kev-27B: 0.00103700108045; OpenThai-SystemOne: 0.00116280492877; WEV-8B: 0.0024069288582; CLEF Flash (Cloudflare): 0.003206195; Lumma-Fev-4B: 0.01744319022; WEV-4B: 0.032238337185; Circuit-1.7B: 0.051119339816; Kev-9B: 0.0600035897649; WEV-1.7B: 0.0808692659754; Kev-4B: 0.0853379972446; MoJev: 0.104382791427; AgentJev: 0.222490954627; Laya: 0.394375336201; VerQen: 0.520406265727; Fragment-2: 0.954978718067. A separate panel shows only the 11 models with 12/12 accuracy, on a linear 0 to 0.06 scale.
svg.text: How close were the probabilities to the labels?
All five choices count · Mean over 12 labeled answers · Lower is better
Choice Brier · full 0–2 scale · lowest first
Labels are rounded to eight decimal places; the saved data retains full precision.
Independent linear 0–0.06 scale · Sorted by Brier within this captured sample
Choice Brier · detail 0–0.06 scale · lowest first
Perfect accuracy can conceal different probability quality. Brier is not an accuracy percentage.
One small run cannot establish calibration or a universal model ranking.
